case_pprz.title: Paparazzi
case_pprz.lead: The first project launched under the partnership model: we built the entire online sales system — from the storefront to the admin panel — with no upfront fee.

sections.title: Overview
p: Paparazzi is a photo and video equipment store with thousands of products: cameras, lenses, lighting, audio and accessories. The team needed a fast, modern store that works with real stock and prices — without manual routine.
We took the entire technical side on us: designed, built and launched the system as a whole — the website, the catalogue, the cart and checkout, the customer account and the store management panel.

sections.title: Storefront & catalogue
p: A catalogue with cascading categories, filters by brand, availability and price, promo badges for discounts and new arrivals, product comparison and a wishlist. Light and dark themes out of the box.

sections.title: Product page
p: The product card shows per-store availability, cashback, Trade-in and extra services — from equipment setup to a personal lesson. Reviews, ratings and related products help people buy with confidence.

sections.title: Management panel
p: The team manages content without developers: banners, promos, top sellers, new arrivals, pages. Discounted products are edited in bulk — prices recalculate instantly.

sections.title: Inventory sync
p: Over 27 thousand products stay in sync with the BAS accounting system: prices, stock and new items update automatically. The admin panel only edits what belongs to the storefront — categories, visibility and the “Top seller” and “New” flags.

sections.title: Result
p: The store lives on its new domain paparazzi.shop and keeps evolving every month: we continue working on sales growth, because we earn a percentage of it — that is the essence of the partnership model.

layers.title: The website is only the [visible part]
layers.p1: Customers see the catalogue, product pages and checkout. But every purchase depends on a much larger process behind the scenes.
layers.p2: The order needs to reach the CRM. A manager should see it immediately and contact the customer. Payment information needs to be recorded. Inventory needs to update. Delivery needs to be arranged. The customer needs to receive a notification. And the business owner needs a clear view of what is happening with sales.
layers.p3: When these processes are disconnected, teams move data manually, orders take longer to process and information inevitably gets lost.
layers.p4: That is why we do not build an isolated website. We create one connected system designed around the way your business actually works.

model.statement: Usually a business pays for development first — and only finds out after launch whether the product works. We offer a different model: we build the system with no upfront fee and receive an agreed percentage of sales after launch. Our compensation begins when real sales begin.
model.title: Development without the [upfront cost]
model.p1: In the traditional model, a business pays for design and development first and only finds out after launch how well the new product works in practice.
model.p3: Overdone takes on the technical development without charging an upfront development fee. After launch, we receive an agreed percentage of the sales processed through the system we created.
model.p4: You are not paying for a number of hours, designs or lines of code. Our compensation begins when real sales begin.
model.p5: That gives us a direct reason to build a product that works well for both your customers and your team — not simply to complete the development scope.

items.q: Do I need to pay for development before launch?
items.a:
No. There is no upfront fee for product design and development.

The project may still involve external costs, such as service licences, hosting, payment providers, infrastructure or content production. These are discussed separately before work begins.
We calculate it after reviewing the business. It depends on margins, sales volume, the complexity of the technical solution and the level of our team’s involvement after launch.

The percentage is calculated from completed orders processed through the e-commerce system we create.

The treatment of returns, cancellations, partial payments and other non-standard transactions is defined in the agreement in advance.

items.q: Can you connect our existing CRM?
items.a:
Yes. If the current CRM is suitable for the future process, we integrate it with the new system.

If it limits the business or does not cover the required tasks, we can help select and implement a more suitable solution.

items.q: Can you rebuild an existing online store?
items.a: Yes. We can create a new product from scratch or rebuild an existing website and the processes connected to it.

items.q: Who owns the product and source code?
items.a: Ownership of the product, source code, infrastructure and development deliverables is defined in the partnership agreement before work begins.

items.q: How long does the revenue-share model last?
items.a: The term is agreed individually and depends on the development scope, business economics and Overdone’s ongoing involvement.
